ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information; Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act; Commercial Act (Sangbeop) Art. 287 et seq.; Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information; Financial Services Commission and Financial Supervisory Service AML/CFT regulations; Korea's implementation of FATF standards, including registration duties under the Act on Registration of Real Estate under Real Name and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) guidance on beneficial ownership transparency.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Korean Registry Office (Deung-gi-won)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court Registration Office / District Court Registry Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued domestically in Korean; if submitted abroad, obtain a certified true copy from the registry, have it notarized by a Korean notary public, then obtain a Hague Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs (for Apostille Convention member states); for non-member states, after notarization obtain consular legalization from the Korean consulate and the destination state's embassy/consulate in Korea

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Sealed Corporate Registry) issued by the Korean Registry Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court Registration Office / District Court Registry Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Korean domestic issuance; notarize the certified extract and then apply to the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for a Hague Apostille for Apostille Convention states; for non-convention states, process through consular legalization by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the relevant foreign consulate in Korea

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation and the opening of bank accounts, signed by the beneficial owner(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in Korea or foreign originator notary, depending on the corporate seat of the beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the beneficial owner is Korean: notarize the resolution and obtain an Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Hague states) or consular legalization (non-Hague states). If the beneficial owner is foreign: notarize in the country of origin, obtain an Apostille in that country for Korea if it is an Apostille state, or obtain Korean consular legalization and the relevant Korean administrative certification if the origin country is not an Apostille state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Jang Yu Gyeol Jeong) certified by the incorporating Korean attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean licensed attorney (lawyer) certifying the final internal version, with the original registered with the Korean Registry Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authenticate the certified Articles of Association copy by notarization and issue a Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille for Apostille member states; for non-member states, obtain consular legalization from the Korean consulate in the receiving country or from the foreign consulate in Korea after Korean MOFA legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a Korean or global bank confirming account conduct, KYC verification, and no adverse history
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank or financial institution maintaining the applicant's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued on bank letterhead and authenticated by the issuing bank's authorized signatory; if required outside Korea, the bank document must be notarized and then receive a Hague Apostille from the apostille authority of the issuing bank's jurisdiction (if an Apostille Convention state) or be legalized through the consular channel of the destination state and, where applicable, the Korean consulate

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every prospective director, shareholder holding 25% or more, senior officer, and controlling founder must undergo real-time screening against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) suspicious transaction reporting and current UN Security Council sanctions lists, the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Sectoral Sanctions lists, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UK OFSI list, and Korea's own publicly announced financial action task force-based domestic sanctions and restricted transaction notices. The compliance protocol requires source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification for all beneficial owners, enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons or family members/significant associates, negative news and adverse-media checks covering the past five years, and continuous monitoring of all bank and shareholder relationships for the life of the corporate entity, with mandatory filing of a suspicious transaction report to KoFIU within three business days of detection of any match, unusual activity, or red flag under the Specific Financial Information Act and FATF recommendations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Commercial Registration Information System (Commercial Registry, Supreme Court of Korea) and the e-Returns service of the Korean Tax Authority (HomeTax) for business registration name verification
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The approved corporate name must be stated in Hangul; where a foreign-language or English name is used in parallel it must be a phonetic transliteration or registered exceptional rendering acceptable to the Korean Registry, and the name must contain 'Chusik Hoesa' or the statutory equivalent 'Chusikhoesa' to indicate a stock corporation. Four-tier naming conventions require the distinctive word, business characteristic, corporate form, and limitation markers to be arranged in accordance with Articles 19 and 23 of the Commercial Act and Supreme Court Registration Practice Guideline; a name identical with an existing domestic company or a registered trademark is prohibited, and names that may mislead as to a government agency, foreign state, international organization, or the nature of the corporation are subject to rejection unless ministerial or sectoral approval is obtained.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receipt of a formal registry rejection the applicant attorney must within seven business days submit a written administrative appeal or objection to the head of the relevant District Court Registry Office or the Supreme Court Registration Division, attaching the entity formation documents, the proposed name, evidence of trademark clearance or right to use the same where applicable, and a statutory interpretation showing conformity with Commercial Act Articles 19 and 23 and the Registration Practice Guidelines. The appeal must describe the negative registry decision number and issue date, set out the corrected name or argue why the original name is not forbidden, and propose a fallback alternative. If the registry remains silent or issues a second rejection, the applicant shall proceed to the Administrative Litigation Act procedure before the competent administrative court within ninety days, while simultaneously re-applying for a reserved alternative name to avoid delay of the incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox will not satisfy the Korean Commercial Act's requirement of a precise registered office address for service of process, tax collection, and supervisory inspection, and is expressly unsuitable for a payment gateway or electronic financial business applicant subject to the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and Financial Services Commission supervision. The Korean tax service and banks generally reject a non-physical mail-forwarding address or coworking mailing address for this industry, as the business requires a registered head office where corporate books, minutes, AML/CFT compliance files, and PSP transaction and audit records are physically maintained and where an authorized compliance officer exists. A serviced office with exclusive or dedicated office space under a term lease, an on-site Korean corporate secretary, a physical signboard, and local employees or personnel can meet substance requirements, but a co-working space or virtual office without a dedicated lease and local operational presence is not compliant for the supervised payment gateway and merchant acquiring business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) the registered office must have a visible Korean-language sign or plaque identifying the company; (2) on-site presence of corporate minute books, shareholder register, AML/CFT manual, business license, and PSP licenses or pending application records; (3) availability of an officer or employee who can explain fundamental operations; and (4) physical bill invoices or lease agreements for the premises. The likelihood of an unannounced on-site inspection by the Korean Registry or municipal tax official during the first year is high-risk if the company is classified as a high-risk under Financial Services Commission guidance, and the probability is quantified as greater than 65% for a cross-border payment gateway with initial monthly settlement flows, while routine postal or desk audits occur in nearly every formation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, specifically Articles 288 to 328 (incorporation, share capital, board of directors, and registration), Articles 295 and 317 (subscription and incorporation registration), Article 393 (board powers), and Article 409 (auditor independence), together with the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, Articles 2(1)(3), 28, and 34-38, for the payment gateway licensing regime.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registration Information Center (iROs) of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office, operated by the National Court Administration of the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Registration Application, statutory registration notice, and certified copy of registration (Seollib Deunggi) under the Registration of Real Estate Act and the Commercial Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: General incorporation: None under the Korean Commercial Act. However, for the payment gateway / electronic financial business license, the FSC requires minimum paid-in capital of at least KRW 1,000,000,000 (approximately USD 740,000), which must be fully paid into a blocked pre-incorporation escrow account at a Korean bank before court registration and FSC registration; no withdrawal is permitted until the certificate of incorporation is issued, and higher equity may be required depending on settlement volume and foreign-exchange exposure.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, at the First Board of Directors meeting of [Company Name], a Chusik Hoesa being formed under the Republic of Korea Commercial Act, that the following governance and formation resolutions are adopted, effective immediately, and shall be entered in the corporation's minute book:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The Board ratifies the subscription of the entire authorized share capital, [number] shares of par value [amount] each, into the name of each subscriber as set forth in the founders' subscription application. The Board acknowledges that all issued shares have been subscribed and will be fully paid before court registration. The Board instructs the Representative Director to obtain the capital deposit certificate from the escrow bank and to deposit the paid-in capital in the blocked pre-incorporation account, from which no withdrawal shall be made prior to the issuance of the certificate of incorporation except as permitted by law.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board approves the opening of operating accounts, settlement accounts, and segregated fiduciary float accounts with [Bank Name] to receive card settlement proceeds, gateway fees, merchant float, and cross-border remittance. The Board authorizes the Representative Director, Chief Finance Officer, and Compliance Officer, collectively for amounts above [amount] and individually for routine operations, to execute account documents, sign foreign exchange and payment-network agreements, and give bank instructions subject to the corporation's anti-money laundering and sanctions policies. Any account change shall require a further board resolution.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE. The Board adopts [address] as the registered office and principal place of business in the Republic of Korea. The Board directs management to register the office with the District Court Registry, to file the business registration with the National Tax Service, and to notify the Financial Services Commission of the registered address, with any subsequent address change to be approved by the Board and filed in a statutory amendment registration.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The Board appoints [name] as Representative Director, [name] as Chief Finance Officer, [name] as Compliance Officer, and [name] as Auditor, each for the statutory term or until successors are validly elected. The Board confirms that the appointed Auditor satisfies the independence requirements of Article 409 of the Commercial Act. Each appointee signs a notice of acceptance of office, which will be filed with the court registry.

5. GOVERNANCE AND REGULATORY LICENSE. The Board delegates to the Compliance Officer, under the supervision of the Chief Executive Officer, all necessary authority to prepare and submit the Electronic Financial Business registration as a payment gateway under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, to coordinate with the Financial Supervisory Service, to register as an information-reporting entity with the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit, and to implement the required AML/CFT internal controls. The Board authorizes all officers to execute the statutory declarations, applications, and supporting undertakings required by the Financial Services Commission.

This resolution constitutes an authentic act of the Board and may be relied upon by any bank, government authority, or counterparty as evidence of the Board's approval. The Chairperson shall sign and certify a copy of these minutes, and a certified copy shall be transmitted to the court registry, the tax office, and such other authorities as are required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Notary Public under the Korean Notary Act, with online appointment through the notary's office; the resulting notarial certificate will be filed with the District Court Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Korean or with an official English translation, including corporate purpose, share classes, number of authorized shares, par value, board terms, fiscal year, capital structure, and payment gateway business objects. All founders must appear before the notary, prove identity, and affix their signatures and seals. Foreign founders must produce apostilled identity documents and, if a corporate entity, apostilled board resolution and an irrevocable power of attorney to the Korean formation agent. The notary will verify legal capacity and notarize the articles. Any article inconsistent with Financial Services Commission licensing requirements must be redrafted and notarized again before the registration stage.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Founder identity documents and corporate seals
Apostilled or consular-legalized proof of identity/existence for foreign shareholders
Power of attorney to local attorney/formation agent
Registered office lease intent or title certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses or demands additional proof, cure by submitting a certified Korean translation, securing a fresh corporate resolution, or re-notarizing after correcting the required articles; if a defect remains, choose a notary qualified in commercial registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription and Blocked Escrow Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FSC-licensed commercial bank in Korea, authorized to issue capital deposit certificates on the pre-incorporation capital escrow account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a pre-incorporation escrow account in the name of the proposed company and deposit the full paid-in capital stated in the notarized articles. For a payment gateway or PG, the deposit must be at least KRW 1 billion, and the account must be blocked so that no disbursement occurs before the court registration certificate is issued. The bank will perform source-of-funds due diligence and, once satisfied, issue a capital deposit certificate identifying the depositor, the corporate name as beneficiary, the amount, date, and blocked status. The certificate is a mandatory attachment for the incorporation registration and later FSC license application. After incorporation, capital withdrawal is subject to the Commercial Act's capital maintenance and creditor-protection rules.
required_dossiers: Pre-incorporation escrow account application
Notarized articles of incorporation
Founder and subscriber KYC forms
Source of funds and bank statements
Beneficial ownership and AML declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank suspends the account opening under internal anti-money-laundering risk controls, provide enhanced due-diligence materials, authenticated wire-transfer traces, and updated corporate resolutions; if the bank remains unwilling, choose another FSC-licensed bank and document the request and denial for regulatory disclosure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory General Meeting and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inaugural General Shareholders' Meeting presided over by the founders; the adopted minutes and First Board Resolution will be submitted to the District Court Registry and the Financial Services Commission.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the capital deposit certificate is issued, convene the inaugural general shareholders' meeting to approve the articles, issue shares, and elect directors and an auditor. The directors then convene the first board meeting to pass the pro-forma resolution on capital subscription, banking authorization, registered office, officer appointments, and regulatory license delegation. The minute keeper must record the date, place, attending directors, quorum, and voting results. The chairperson and directors sign the minutes. Prepare written consents of the directors and auditor accepting the appointment. The minutes and consents become part of the statutory registration file.
required_dossiers: Convening notice or waiver of notice
Minutes of inaugural general shareholders' meeting
First Board Resolution minutes
Director and auditor consents
Share subscription register
Capital deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry challenges the meeting notification or director election due to a notice or quorum defect, re-convene the general meeting to ratify the action and amend the minutes before registration; if any officer appointment is invalid, replace the officer by a corrective resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Court Registration Division of the court having jurisdiction over the registered office, with subscription filing through the Court Registration Information Center (iROs; www.iros.go.kr).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the corporate meetings, submit the incorporation registration application to the competent district court registry through an attorney or using the iROs portal. The registry checks the notarized articles, capital deposit certificate, minutes, officer consents, registered-office attestation, and registration tax payment. Pay the registration tax and local education surcharge at the court fee window. Once the registration officer enters the company into the commercial register, the certificate of incorporation is issued; the company exists as a legal person from that moment. The attorney should then obtain certified copies of the register and the corporate seal attestation for the opening of post-incorporation government processes.
required_dossiers: Incorporation registration application
Notarized articles
Capital deposit certificate
Minutes of general meeting and first board meeting
Consents of directors and auditor
Proof of registered office, being a lease or title certificate
Registration tax payment receipt
Power of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration officer issues a correction order, supplement the application within two weeks by filing a written response, replace invalid attachments, and pay any fee shortfall; if the registration is rejected, request a written decision and file an administrative objection with the district court within two weeks.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) Hometax portal (www.hometax.go.kr) and the local district tax office of the registered address.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after court registration, file the corporate business registration application and obtain the business registration certificate and business identification number. Register the corporate seal with the competent registration office and obtain the seal certificate, then apply for the electronic certificate for corporate taxpayer authentication. Submitting through Hometax requires the authorized ID of the representative director or a tax representative. This registration enables the company to issue value-added-tax invoices, pay corporate income tax, report withholding on salaries, and transact with financial institutions. The tax office may require the lessor's consent or a financing registration if the office is in a shared business lounge.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation from court registry
Notarized articles
Lease contract or ownership certificate
Representative director ID and corporate seal
Business registration application form
Corporate seal registration certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS rejects or asks for foreign officer details, correct the tax representative appointment, provide a valid lease contract, or amend the address through the Hometax correction function within two weeks; if a penalty is proposed, apply for self-correction to reduce it before assessment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Financial Business License and AML Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) Electronic Financial Business Registration Division, with parallel filing to the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and file the electronic financial business registration application for a payment gateway, classified as an electronic payment settlement agency, under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act. The FSC reviews corporate status, paid-in capital, shareholder structure, management fitness, AML/CFT compliance, system security, settlement segregation, and foreign-exchange handling. The application must include the new business registration certificate, court-issued certificates, capital deposit proof, an AML manual, a sanctions-screening protocol, an IT security implementation plan, and the compliance officer appointment resolution. After initial filing, the FSS will perform an examination. No merchant acquisition, clearing or settlement may be offered until the registration certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: Electronic financial business registration application form
Corporate registration certificate and business registration certificate
Paid-in capital proof and capital deposit certificate
AML/CFT internal control manual and risk assessment
IT security and ISMS certification or security plan
Foreign exchange handling plan for cross-border rails
Compliance officer appointment and organization chart
Audited financial statements and any required fidelity bond
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSC submits a deficiency letter or corrective order, respond within twenty days with supplementary documentation, increased capital, strengthened internal controls, or revised transaction flow design; if the license is denied, use the FSC appeal body and ultimately the Administrative Court.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a domestic Chusik Hoesa, business registration must be filed with the NTS within 20 days from business commencement. For a foreign non-resident entity establishing Korean VAT or corporate tax obligations, the foreign company or its appointed tax representative files a Business Registration Application through HomeTax or at the district tax office having jurisdiction over the domestic place of business. Supporting documents include the company's certificate of incorporation, articles of association or bylaws, board resolution appointing the Korean or tax representative, lease or ownership evidence for the fixed domestic business premises, and an apostilled or consular-legalized home-country registration certificate plus the responsible officer's passport. Upon validation, NTS issues the Business Registration Certificate containing a 10-digit Business Registration Number that simultaneously operates as the corporate TIN and VAT registration number. A foreign non-resident supplier of electronic or digital services without a domestic fixed place of business must register under the VAT Act's simplified non-resident registration procedure and must appoint a tax representative; NTS then issues a non-resident VAT registration number. Separately, for export and import physical goods movements, the entity must register with the Korea Customs Service to obtain a customs importer/exporter registration identifier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election or a general hybrid classification election; a Chusik Hoesa is per se subject to entity-level Korean corporate income tax. The Korean Corporate Tax Act's consolidated taxation for eligible domestic groups is a separate elective filing regime, not an entity classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general monetary turnover threshold for VAT registration; every person making taxable supplies in Korea must register from the first taxable transaction. Domestic small suppliers whose annual taxable turnover is not more than KRW 80,000,000 may use the simplified VAT taxpayer regime, which affects return filing and calculation but does not defer or remove the VAT registration obligation. Foreign non-resident suppliers of digital and electronic services to Korean consumers are required to register under the non-resident electronic service supply rules when Korean B2C supplies can be reasonably expected.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The NTS operates the mandatory HomeTax electronic tax invoice (e-Tax Invoice) system. Every VAT-registered business must issue tax invoices electronically through HomeTax, either via the HomeTax web portal or via the NTS-certified API channel. E-Tax Invoice data is transmitted to NTS at the time of issuance, operating as real-time fiscal reporting and generating the NTS-controlled invoice number and digital integrity markers. There is no independent private fiscal stamping vendor; the HomeTax e-Tax Invoice number and validation chain constitute the anti-fraud control. For consumer B2C transactions, suppliers must also issue cash receipts through the HomeTax cash-receipt system where a consumer requests one or where the transaction is mandatory under the cash-receipt rules. Late issuance or failure to transmit e-Tax Invoices may trigger VAT penalty surcharges under the VAT Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated exports are available under the Korean VAT Act for goods physically exported from Korea and for qualifying services supplied to non-resident recipients and used outside Korea. For goods, title and risk must pass to a foreign buyer, the goods must be cleared through Korea Customs Service as exports, and the outward movement must be supported by shipping documents. For the cross-border payment gateway service, zero-rating is available if the recipient is a non-resident merchant, acquirer, or payment institution, the service is performed in Korea but is not consumed or utilized in Korea, the recipient has no domestic place of business, and the consideration is settled in foreign currency through Korean foreign exchange reporting channels. The service is taxable at 10% where it is effectively supplied for Korean domestic merchants or Korean cardholder settlement activities that lack a genuine overseas supply character.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration Certificate (export clearance confirmation issued by the Korea Customs Service)
Bill of Lading or sea/air waybill evidencing physical export movement
Cross-border payment gateway service contract or merchant agreement showing the non-resident recipient and offshore usage of the service
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign currency receipt confirmation issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS will retrospectively reverse zero-rating and claw back the VAT benefit if the export declaration, bill of lading, service contract, or foreign-exchange receipt documentation is missing, false, late, or internally inconsistent. The company would then be assessed standard VAT at 10% on the full supply value plus statutory penalty surcharges and interest. Penalty surcharges apply under the VAT Act for failure to register, failure to issue an e-Tax Invoice, issuance of false tax invoices, and failure to report the taxable export; aggregate penalty surcharges can reach up to 30%-40% of the tax involved in severe cases. Fraudulent zero-rating or refund claims are additionally prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying criminal fines and imprisonment, and the statutory retroactive assessment period for fraud is ten years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), acting with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the foreign exchange administrator under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and with the Financial Services Commission (FSC) as the licensing authority for electronic payment service providers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won is fully convertible for current-account transactions, while capital-account transactions are governed by a declaration and monitoring regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Merchant acquiring, cross-border digital content settlement, and online payment gateway service fees are current-account services when supported by genuine commercial contracts, invoices, and SRV-related documentation; these flows may be freely converted into KRW at market rates through a licensed domestic foreign exchange bank. Inbound equity and loan capital into a Chusik Hoesa requires a formal foreign investment report and registration procedure before the funds can be recognised as verified paid-in capital; the remittance must pass through a Korean foreign exchange bank with the correct inward remittance purpose code. Dividend remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted after tax withholding, using the applicable treaty rate, but the bank will require evidence of audited retained earnings, the foreign investment registration certificate, and tax clearance. There is no general mandatory surrender of export proceeds to KRW; export receipts may be retained in foreign currency accounts for the statutory settlement window. Non-resident fintech companies and unlicensed offshore EMIs cannot access the Korean won clearing system, and all KRW settlement must occur through domestic banks interconnected with the Korea Financial Telecommunications and Clearings Institute (KFTC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds under current Korean foreign exchange rules; exporters may lawfully hold receivables in foreign currency accounts. However, the statutory settlement requirement dictates that export goods or digital export service earnings must be collected and settled through a licensed domestic foreign exchange bank within 12 months from the date of export or service performance, unless an extension is approved by the relevant bank. The exporter must file transaction reports and retain the underlying commercial invoices, waybills, contracts, and payment receipts for BOK or MOEF examination. For PSP cross-border collections, each receipt should be reconcilable to an underlying merchant transaction record, with the foreign exchange bank issuing a purchase/sale confirmation certificate for each conversion.

Capital Escrow Account and Payment Gateway Merchant Settlement Account
Foreign Currency USD/KRW Account and Cross-Border Disbursement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs such as global payment platforms are not viable as the primary banking layer for a Korean-domiciled Chusik Hoesa. An offshore EMI is not licensed by the Financial Services Commission under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act or the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and it cannot directly access KRW clearing, issue foreign exchange certifications, or perform the statutory reporting functions of a Korean foreign exchange bank. The Korean payment gateway must maintain its operating, escrow, and settlement accounts at a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank connected to KFTC, with cross-border flows settled through SWIFT/CHIPS/Fedwire. An EMI may only be used as a supplementary receive-only wallet for selected overseas merchant collections, subject to the ultimate clearance of funds through a licensed domestic bank; it cannot act as the compliance anchor for Korean foreign exchange regulation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-branch physical presence is required for at least one statutory director, the signatory with actual control, and the underlying ultimate beneficial owner during initial corporate account onboarding. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally available for operational KRW and foreign exchange accounts; Korean AML rules require direct interview and verification of identity documents, passport, proof of foreign address, business licence, corporate registration certificate, and the corporate seal or authorised signatory records. A video pre-screen may be allowed, but the final KYC interview and wet-ink or financial institution-approved electronic signature must be completed in a Korean branch. A foreign director may appoint an in-country attorney through an apostilled and notarised power of attorney, but the bank compliance committee typically requires the principal director to perform the first in-person interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner located in a multiple-layer offshore jurisdiction with opaque corporate shareholders, raising unverified source of wealth concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate structure chart showing every legal holder to natural person, certificate of incumbency from each intermediary entity, passport copies and address verification of all UBOs, 12-month source-of-wealth file including employment confirmation, dividend vouchers, asset sale deeds, audited investor financial statements, foreign tax residence certificates, and a signed beneficial ownership declaration confirming no bearer shares, no nominee shareholders, and no undisclosed custodial arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment aggregation business model with high-volume, low-value cross-border digital transactions, creating suspicion of unlicensed third-party sub-merchant onboarding and potential money mule facilitation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete merchant underwriting and AML programme regardless of the sub-merchant model; PCI DSS Level 1 certificate; ISO 27001 information security certificate; sample merchant agreement with clear prohibited business list; transaction monitoring rules and velocity/threshold settings; sanctions and PEP screening log; independent anti-money laundering audit report from a licensed external auditor; and verified KYC files for the top five merchants by transaction volume.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from an offshore related company where the remittance reference is unclear and the bank cannot confirm the economic substance of the foreign investor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign investment agreement or share subscription contract, board resolution of the investing entity, bank reference letter from the remitting bank, certified source of funds report for the equity amount, latest two-year audited financial statements of the investor, trial balance or dividend distribution minutes supporting accumulated wealth, tax residence certificate, corporate registration extract, and the completed foreign investment report to MOEF or the delegated foreign exchange bank before receipt of the remittance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial registry filing reveals partial cash payment, in-kind contribution, or a mismatch between subscribed capital and the capital deposit verification documents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Korean bank-issued capital deposit confirmation showing the full cash amount and depositor identity, formal subscription plan with payment schedule, notarised appraisal report for any in-kind contribution, statutory auditor or CPA statement verifying that share capital is fully paid and no fictitious capital exists, updated corporate register extract from the local court, and a bank certificate confirming the transfer from the capital escrow account to the operating account after capital verification.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity and shareholder loan funding must be routed by SWIFT MT103 to a foreign currency bank account in the name of the Chusik Hoesa or the foreign investor at a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank. The remitter must include the Korean entity corporate registration number and the approved foreign exchange purpose code for inward direct investment or equity contribution. The receiving bank will verify the remittance, issue a foreign exchange purchase or capital deposit certificate, and require the prescribed foreign investment report to be filed with MOEF through KOTRA or the delegated foreign exchange bank. Once the bank confirms the capital deposit and the Commercial Court issues the final corporate register amendment, the escrowed capital can be converted into KRW and moved to the operational account. Capital verification in Korea requires the deposit of cash, the issuing bank's confirmation, and a statutory auditor review where required; the foreign investor must retain the foreign investment registration certificate for all future dividend remittances and capital return purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For physical goods-related payments, the company may use SWIFT MT103 for simple wire settlements, commercial letters of credit for supplier credit, and documentary collections where the merchant requires transport-document-linked payment. For digital content licensing, software subscription, and cross-border payment gateway service fees, the dominant compliant clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 through the domestic foreign exchange bank, supported by service agreements, invoices, and tax withholding certificates where applicable. USD clearing in the United States will be completed via Fedwire or CHIPS through a correspondent account of the Korean bank, while Visa and Mastercard settlement flows come into the acquiring account through the card network and are then transferred to the operating account after merchant fees and FX conversion. Domestic disbursements to Korean merchants are executed through KFTC wire or ACK settlement; the PSP must maintain an escrow ledger and reconcile every disbursement against a controlled merchant account file.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts up to 12 months with a licensed Korean dealing bank, limited to documented trade and merchant settlement exposure, subject to the bank's real demand rule and monthly reporting to the BOK.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted for KRW/USD hedge purposes only where the PSP holds confirmed cross-border merchant settlement receivables or foreign currency liabilities; cash-settled in KRW and reported as granular forward trade data to the counterparty bank and BOK.

Cross-currency swaps available for long-term foreign currency debt or shareholder loan exposure with a demonstrable underlying transaction, prior foreign exchange reporting, and explicit approval of the domestic dealing bank; naked speculative derivative positions are prohibited.
Simple FX spots used for immediate merchant settlement conversions, executed through the domestic foreign exchange bank and captured on the bank's foreign exchange transaction reporting system.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting of shareholders; convening, quorum, and approval of financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korean Commercial Act Articles 365 and 446; ordinary annual meeting documents are not filed with a commercial registry but minutes and financial statements must be retained on site. If the company is within the external audit regime, the approved financial statements and external audit report must be transmitted to the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) after the meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three calendar months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year end, the meeting must be held by March 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to convene the annual shareholders' meeting within the statutory window are subject to an administrative fine of up to KRW 5,000,000 (approximately USD 3,846); continued failure to act may result in a court order requiring the meeting to be held, and, in extreme cases, court-ordered compulsory examination or dissolution remedies under the Korean Commercial Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and corporate tax settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea through the HomeTax electronic filing system; corporate tax returns are statutory annual filings separate from corporate registry maintenance.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year end; for a December 31 fiscal year end, filing and payment are due by March 31 of the following year. If the return is prepared by a licensed certified tax accountant, the filing deadline is automatically extended by one month to April 30, but the tax payment deadline is not extended.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file, underreporting, or fraudulent reporting triggers an additional tax of 20% to 40% of the suppressed corporate tax; late payment interest accrues at 0.022% per day (approximately 8.03% per annum) from the original due date until full payment. Persistent delinquency can lead to attachment and seizure of assets by the NTS, compulsory collection, and criminal referral for willful tax evasion under the Framework Act on National Taxes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit report and audited financial statements submission under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) of South Korea, filed through the DART electronic disclosure system and, where applicable, made available to the National Tax Service.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The external auditor must issue and submit the audit report to the company no later than three weeks before the annual general meeting; the company must file the audit report and the approved audited financial statements with the FSS/SFC no later than two weeks after the shareholders' meeting approval. For a December 31 fiscal year, the practical file date is anchored to the March 31 annual meeting and typically falls by mid-April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint a statutory auditor or to file the audit report allows the SFC to impose corrective orders and designate an external auditor, and exposes directors to administrative fines under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies. For a regulated payment gateway, a material audit filing failure can trigger the suspension or revocation of the online payment service and cross-border payment license by the Financial Services Commission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Payment Service Provider regulatory report and AML compliance report under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) and Financial Supervisory Service (FSS); AML and suspicious transaction reports are transmitted to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual business report and related regulatory report must be filed with the FSS/KoFIU within two months after the fiscal year end, by February 28 or February 29 for a December 31 fiscal year end. Suspicious transaction reports under the FIU Act are event-driven and must be filed within the statutory reporting window from detection; large cash transaction reports are due within 30 days of the calendar reporting month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False, defective, or missing filings attract administrative fines up to KRW 50,000,000 (approximately USD 38,462) under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act; continued non-compliance may trigger license suspension or revocation of the payment gateway authorization, and knowing AML reporting violations may result in criminal penalties and personal director liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign investment and ultimate beneficial owner status; annual foreign investment business status report for non-resident shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any share transfer, change in registered foreign investment status, or change in ultimate beneficial ownership that affects a registered foreign investor must be reported to KOTRA within 30 days of the event. In addition, a registered foreign-invested company must submit the annual foreign investment business status report for the prior fiscal year by March 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted UBO and shareholding-change reports carry administrative fines of up to KRW 5,000,000 (approximately USD 3,846) under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; in restricted industries, non-reporting can result in forfeiture of foreign investment registration benefits, tax incentives, and daily compounding penalties, and may expose directors to personal liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Korean Chusik Hoesa is subject to compulsory independent CPA audit under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies if any of the following criteria is satisfied: (a) the company is listed on KOSPI or KOSDAQ, or is otherwise a public-interest entity; (b) the company is a financial company under specialized financial statutes, which includes licensed electronic financial business operators such as online merchant-acquiring platforms and cross-border payment gateways supervised by the FSC and FSS, regardless of asset size; (c) the company is an unlisted non-financial stock company with total assets of KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9,230,769) or more at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year; or (d) the Securities and Futures Commission formally designates the company for external audit because of public interest, investor protection, or regulatory restructuring concerns. Korean law does not use turnover or headcount as the exclusive mandatory audit trigger; the controlling quantitative trigger is total assets, while licensed PSP and payment gateway entities are always auditable because of their financial-company status.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The governing accounting framework is Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for listed companies, financial companies, and public-interest entities; unlisted non-financial companies that do not clearly fall under K-IFRS may apply Korean GAAP as issued by the Korea Accounting Institute. All statutory audits are performed in accordance with Korean Standards on Auditing (KSA), which are aligned with the international standards of the IAASB.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korean law does not impose a general annual UBO filing for every domestic stock company. The operative rule for the Chusik Hoesa is the 30-day change-driven reporting protocol: any allotment or transfer of shares that gives a non-resident a 10% or greater registered or beneficial ownership stake, or any material change to an existing foreign investment registration, must be filed with KOTRA through the Foreign Investment Support Center within 30 days. The company must simultaneously update the Register of Members and reflect the transfer in its corporate books. On an annual basis, a registered foreign-invested company must file the annual foreign investment business status report with KOTRA by March 31 for the prior fiscal year, covering capital, revenue, employment, dividends, and foreign-exchange matters. For AML purposes, the company must maintain current customer and beneficial-owner due-diligence records under the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Information, and these records must be available for on-site inspection by the FSS and KoFIU during annual supervision of the payment gateway license.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - USD 2,200 per year for a registered office address, registered agent services, physical correspondence handling, and corporate secretarial record maintenance in Seoul for a non-resident-owned Korean stock company.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 15,000 - USD 55,000 per year for a certified CPA audit of a cross-border online payment gateway PSP with AML controls, foreign-currency reserve book examination, and K-IFRS reporting, depending on transaction volume and the complexity of the statutory registers.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top national corporate income tax bracket on taxable income exceeding KRW 300,000,000,000, with progressive brackets of 9%, 19%, 21% and 24%; plus 10% local corporate income tax surtax, producing an aggregate combined top rate of 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying foreign-invested high-tech enterprises in Free Economic Zones or Foreign Investment Zones may obtain a 100% corporate tax holiday for 5 years and a 50% reduction for the following 2 years; R&D expenditure tax credits of up to 20-30% are available for qualifying technology and scientific development; job creation tax credits and investment tax credits may further lower the effective rate; Korea does not operate a general patent box, but qualifying technology transfer income may access reduced tax rates or tax exemption under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return on Tax Base and Tax Calculation (final return under Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Act, including attached financial statements, adjustment schedules, international transaction statements and non-resident withholding schedules); filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax system (www.hometax.go.kr) or through accredited tax-agent e-filing software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return, plus a semi-annual interim prepayment return due within 3 months after the end of each 6-month period of the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual final corporate tax return must be filed within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa the deadline is 31 March; an extension of up to one month may be allowed where financial statements are audited or where an approved tax agent prepares the e-filing, and further extensions may be granted by the relevant district tax office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Taxpayer identification and effective management
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the Korean legal name, Chusik Hoesa registration number, business registration number, representative director, tax identification number, physical address of the head office, fiscal year-end and the principal business code for payment services and merchant acquiring (ISIC 6619 / NAICS 522320).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the ultimate non-resident shareholders and their countries of residence; confirm the place of effective management in Korea; if a non-resident payment gateway parent operates through a Korean entity, attach the Shareholder Register, board resolution approving the Korean filing, and note whether a foreign head office or PE exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Financial statement reconciliation and accounting-to-tax adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Record total assets, total revenue, gross commission income, interchange fees, operating expenses, operating income, non-operating income and expenses, and pre-tax accounting income; then reconcile K-IFRS accounting income to taxable income through permanent and temporary difference schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For cross-border PSP revenue, include merchant acquiring and clearing fees recognized in Korea without netting foreign service fees unless properly documented; add back non-deductible expenses such as excessive entertainment expenses, cash bribes, or payments to non-resident related parties without substance or source withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Taxable income and tax loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the adjusted taxable income by subtracting non-taxable income, adding disallowed expenses, applying temporary difference reversals, and deducting available tax loss carryforwards under Article 13 of the Corporate Tax Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim no more than the statutory 10-year loss carryforward limit; losses of the Korean Chusik Hoesa cannot be transferred to a non-resident parent; if the entity is a conduit or lacks economic substance, tax loss deductions may be denied upon GAAR recharacterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Statutory tax calculation and local surtax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the progressive national corporate tax rates to the taxable income in Box 3 and compute the national corporate income tax; then calculate local corporate income tax surtax equal to 10% of the national corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean-resident Chusik Hoesa, the full tax base is subject to Korean tax on worldwide income; for a non-resident branch, only Korean-source income is taxed and a branch remittance tax may apply; here the Korean entity must report global revenue from its payment gateway business and cannot allocate profits to tax havens without transfer pricing compliance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Tax credits, foreign tax credit and treaty relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report tax credits including R&D tax credit, job creation tax credit, foreign tax credit, and any investment tax credit; compute the minimum tax limit and final national tax after credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Foreign Tax Credit schedules for any Korean-source income taxed abroad; if a DTA reduces the Korean withholding tax on outbound payments, attach the relevant treaty applications and do not claim a foreign tax credit for the treaty-exempt amount; non-resident shareholders cannot claim Korean personal credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Non-resident withholding tax reconciliation on outbound dividends, interest, and royalties
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List all gross amounts paid or credited to non-resident shareholders or related parties as dividends, interest, royalties and other cross-border payments; enter the statutory or treaty withholding rate, the amount of tax withheld, and the due date for remittance to the National Tax Service.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each outbound dividend, interest or royalty payment, state the non-resident payee name, country, relationship and Tax Residency Certificate; apply the 22% statutory WHT (20% national plus 2% local) unless a valid DTA application and beneficial ownership declaration are attached; failure to withhold creates personal liability for directors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - International transactions and transfer pricing declarations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose cross-border related-party transactions in the Report on International Transactions attached to the corporate tax return; include intercompany clearing fees, management fees, technical service fees, royalty payments, shareholding percentages and the transfer pricing method applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If intercompany transactions with foreign related parties exceed KRW 10,000,000,000 during the fiscal year, confirm that the Local File and Master File are simultaneously prepared and available; state the arm's length method used (CUP, resale price, cost plus, TNMM or profit split); a missing disclosure flag will expose the entity to adjustments and penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Payment gateway license, AML and economic substance declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the Financial Services Commission registration or license number under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, the principal payment rails operated (Visa, Mastercard, Fedwire), annual cross-border transaction volume, AML compliance program identification, suspicious transaction reporting status, and the number of operational employees in Korea.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide objective evidence of substance in Korea: physical office lease, director board minutes, employees performing real payment-route operations, bank accounts, and risk management; absence of Korean substance may cause the NTS to deny treaty benefits, pierce the corporate veil, or recharacterize the Korean Chusik Hoesa as a conduit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the final corporate tax return attracts additional tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes Articles 47-2 through 47-4; failure to file by the statutory deadline generally adds 20% of the final tax payable, unfaithful non-declaration adds 10% if negligent and 40% if fraudulent, unfaithful under-reporting adds 10% if negligent and 40% if fraudulent, and late payment accrues a daily surcharge of 0.03% on the unpaid amount; criminal tax evasion under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act is punishable by imprisonment of up to 3 years or a fine of up to 30 times the evaded tax, and summary indictment thresholds may apply where the understated tax exceeds statutory limits.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national dividend withholding tax under Article 98 of the Corporate Tax Act plus 2% local income tax surtax under the Local Tax Act), subject to reduction under an applicable tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident payee must obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate from the tax authority of its residence jurisdiction and provide it, together with a duly completed Application for Exemption or Reduction of Withholding Tax under a Tax Treaty and a signed Beneficial Ownership Declaration, to the Korean withholding company before the payment date; for dividends, the beneficial owner must satisfy any minimum shareholding and holding-period condition in the treaty; the Korean company must file the application with the district tax office and obtain approval before applying the reduced rate; if the application is rejected, the full 22% must be withheld and the non-resident may file a correction claim or pursue a mutual agreement procedure under the DTA; substance must be demonstrated under the OECD BEPS MLI principal purpose test and limitation-on-benefits provision to prevent treaty abuse.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on outbound interest and royalties is 22% (20% national tax plus 2% local surtax); under Korean tax treaties the rates are typically reduced to between 5% and 15% depending on the treaty partner, the nature of the intellectual property, and whether the recipient is the beneficial owner; interest derived by unrelated financial institutions may receive lower treaty rates, but royalties and interest paid by a Korean PSP to a related offshore entity must be supported by economic substance and transfer pricing analysis to avoid recharacterization.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10,000,000,000 (KRW 10 billion) in cross-border transactions with foreign related parties in a single business year triggers mandatory preparation of simultaneous transfer pricing documentation, including the Local File and the integrated Report on International Transactions; the Master File is required when the group meets the relevant consolidated revenue threshold under Article 11 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, and Country-by-Country Reporting is required for multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least KRW 1,000,000,000,000 (KRW 1 trillion).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not enforce an annual Economic Substance Regulation filing like certain zero-tax jurisdictions, but the National Tax Service and Korean courts apply a substance-over-form doctrine, the general anti-abuse rule under Article 17 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, and the OECD MLI standards; a Chusik Hoesa operating a cross-border payment gateway must demonstrate Core Income-Generating Activities in Korea, including bank account management, merchant on-boarding, transaction monitoring, risk control, board meetings and operational employees; a shell entity with no Korean decision-making or operational substance will be denied treaty benefits and may be directly recharacterized as an agent or conduit of its foreign parent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Failure to Withhold Cross-Border Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Chusik Hoesa deliberately inflates deductible expenses by issuing fabricated cross-border invoices for fake technical services, underreports merchant acquiring and clearing revenue, and pays out dividends, interest or royalties to a non-resident parent without withholding the statutory 22% tax or without valid treaty relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3(1) imposes imprisonment of up to 3 years or a fine of up to 30 times the evaded tax; the Framework Act on National Taxes adds a 40% fraudulent under-reporting penalty plus a 0.03% daily late-payment surcharge on unpaid tax; the National Tax Service may additionally impose penalties for failure to file withholding schedules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced when a director uses the Chusik Hoesa as a facade for fraud; under Article 39 of the National Tax Collection Act a director may become a secondary taxpayer and be personally liable for unpaid corporate tax and withholding tax if corporate assets are insufficient; directors may face criminal imprisonment for intentional false filing, financial restitution to the tax authority, and a travel ban or departure restriction imposed by the National Tax Service.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Payment Gateway Operation and AML Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The entity operates as an online merchant acquiring, clearing and settlement provider for Visa, Mastercard and Fedwire payment rails without obtaining the required registration or license from the Financial Services Commission under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, and fails to implement customer due diligence, suspicious transaction reporting and wire-transaction record-keeping under the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 49 of the Electronic Financial Transactions Act penalizes unregistered electronic financial business with imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 50,000,000; the Financial Information Act imposes imprisonment of up to 3 years or a fine of up to KRW 30,000,000 for willful AML failures; the Financial Intelligence Unit may impose administrative fines, revoke authorizations, and refer the case to prosecutors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who direct or knowingly permit unlicensed PSP operations are not protected by limited liability; they are jointly and severally liable for restitution of merchant and consumer funds, can be blacklisted by the FIU and Financial Supervisory Service, may face travel bans, and can be convicted of criminal AML offenses with actual imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Conduit or Shell Company Treaty Abuse and Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Chusik Hoesa has no real employees, no physical head office, no local board autonomy and no substantive payment-processing functions, and is used purely as a conduit to channel royalties and dividends to a low-tax jurisdiction; the entity also fails to file the Report on International Transactions, refuses to prepare the Local File and Master File after exceeding the KRW 10 billion related-party threshold, or applies non-arm's length intercompany clearing fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Articles 11 and 13 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, the National Tax Service may disregard the transaction, recharacterize the conduit structure, adjust taxable income on an arm's length basis, and impose an additional tax of 30% for non-compliance with simultaneous documentation requirements or up to the amount of income improperly omitted under GAAR; treaty benefits will be denied under the MLI principal purpose test, restoring the full 22% withholding on outbound payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where directors signed false substance declarations, approved sham contracts, or failed to cause the required TP documentation to be produced, the corporate veil can be pierced; directors face personal civil liability for the resulting corporate tax assessments and penalties, NTS blacklisting and departure restrictions, and criminal liability for tax evasion where the conduit arrangement is found fraudulent, with imprisonment terms available under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.
